spacing.evidence: The divider between picker and summary changes from vertical to horizontal on mobile, preserving the grouping and keeping all five evenly spaced day controls in one row.

typography.evidence: The large italic “tune-ups,” smaller upright serif headings and bold sans-serif weekdays establish distinct roles that remain legible on mobile.

color.evidence: Orange connects the booking button and price badge to the illustrated bicycle crank, while the pale sage background distinguishes the summary from the picker.

accessibility.evidence: Visible radio circles identify the choices, and both browser trees confirm full weekday names, a “Choose a day” group and a status region inside the booking summary.

fidelity.evidence: Second Spin displays 48-hour tune-ups for $85 at 41 Elm Street, spells out Tuesday-to-Saturday availability and pairs those five choices with a summary prompting “Select a day.”

typography.evidence: The bold display serif emphasizes the offer, booking heading and price, while the sans-serif instructions, weekdays and summary details stay readable on mobile.

color.evidence: Burgundy ties the bicycle poster to the booking link and $85 price, and dark weekday labels stand out against the pale buttons at both widths.

accessibility.evidence: Both browser trees give the five radios full weekday names under “Booking day,” with selection feedback evidenced only by the initial “Select a day” summary value.

fidelity.evidence: Second Spin explicitly invites visitors to pick one of the Tuesday-through-Saturday choices to preview a booking, and the summary shows the bike tune-up, $85 price, 48-hour turnaround and 41 Elm Street address.

hierarchy.evidence: The oversized “Field Notes” title identifies the broadcast immediately, and the yellow “Listen live” button stands out beside it on desktop and below the host on mobile.

spacing.evidence: “Weekdays” aligns with the player’s left edge on desktop, and consistent mobile margins keep the stacked player and ruled schedule row aligned.

typography.evidence: The condensed title fits on one line even at 390 pixels, and the bold schedule numerals make “7–9” easy to pick out beside the smaller “am.”

color.evidence: Yellow draws attention to the on-air dot and listening control against navy, while the shift to cream marks the start of the schedule.

accessibility.evidence: Visible “On air” text explains the dot, and both browser trees expose the named “Listen live” button, the “Silent demo” status and the Schedule region.

fidelity.evidence: Low Signal’s nonprofit identity, Field Notes with Ana Reyes and the weekday 7–9 am slot are exact, and “Silent demo” labels the player, though the evidence covers only its initial state.

hierarchy.evidence: The illustrated radio draws the first glance, especially on mobile where the entire poster precedes the show title and the prominent “Listen live” button.

spacing.evidence: The poster and show details sit side by side on desktop and share the same margins on mobile, with a tighter gap grouping the weekday hours and listening control at both widths.

typography.evidence: The serif title shifts from two lines on desktop to one on mobile, preserving the italic emphasis on “Notes” and keeping the bold host name and airtime easy to scan.

color.evidence: Plum connects the radio artwork, station mark and listening control, and the red dot beside “On air” gives broadcast status its own accent.

accessibility.evidence: The broadcast indicator has a readable “On air” label and both browser trees name the “Listen live” button, while the listener status is empty in both initial views.

fidelity.evidence: The station, show, host and weekday hours match the brief, and “Listen live” is clear, though the supplied views give no indication that the demo is silent or how it identifies the listener as live after activation.
